record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Determine whether the transitions between βKT and 1/2βKT in the two-dimensional Coulomb gas are visible in any correlation functions.

evidence.quote: Are the transitions between βKT and 1/2βKT in the D=2 Coulomb gas visible in any correlations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional Coulomb gas: a neutral gas of unit positive and negative point charges in $\mathbb{R}^2$ interacting via the logarithmic (two-dimensional Coulomb) potential $V(x,y) = -\log|x-y|$, with grand-canonical partition function controlled by an inverse temperature $\beta > 0$ and a fugacity $z > 0$ (suitably regularized at short distances). It is known that as $\beta$ varies, the system exhibits a Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless type transition at a critical value $\beta_{KT}$, separating a high-temperature plasma phase (Debye screening, exponential decay of charge correlations) from a low-temperature dipole phase (power-law decay of correlations from bound neutral pairs). Heuristic and renormalization-group analyses suggest the existence of a hierarchy of further transitions at $\beta_{KT}/n$ for integers $n \geq 2$, associated with the unbinding of multipoles of higher charge; in particular at $\beta_{KT}/2$ a transition associated with quadrupole unbinding is predicted.

Question: Determine whether the transitions between $\beta_{KT}$ and $\beta_{KT}/2$ in the two-dimensional Coulomb gas are visible in any correlation function. Specifically, decide whether there exists a (possibly multi-point or higher-charge) correlation function whose asymptotic behavior changes qualitatively as $\beta$ crosses some value in the open interval $(\beta_{KT}/2, \beta_{KT})$, thereby exhibiting an intermediate phase transition between the principal Kosterlitz–Thouless transition at $\beta_{KT}$ and the next predicted transition at $\beta_{KT}/2$.
artifact.category_tag: two-dimensional Coulomb gas and BKT transitions
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether intermediate transitions between $\beta_{KT}$ and $\beta_{KT}/2$ in the 2D Coulomb gas manifest in correlation functions appears to remain open. Rigorous results (Fröhlich–Spencer and subsequent extensions, including recent work on power-law decay above $\beta_{KT}$) establish the principal BKT transition and characterize correlation decay in the dipole phase, but do not exhibit any intermediate transitions in correlation functions in the interval $(\beta_{KT}/2,\beta_{KT})$.

status_evidence.title: Critical exponents of the two dimensional Coulomb gas at the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition
status_evidence.snippet: Along the phase transition curve and for small activity, the long-distance decay of the 'fractional charge' correlation is power law, with a multiplicative logarithmic correction.
status_evidence.claim: Recent rigorous work focuses on critical exponents at $\beta_{KT}$ itself, not on intermediate transitions between $\beta_{KT}$ and $\beta_{KT}/2$.

status_evidence.title: The Kosterlitz-Thouless transition in two-dimensional Abelian spin systems and the Coulomb gas
status_evidence.snippet: For any beta>8π, the two-point external charges correlation function exhibits the power-law falloff characteristic of the Kosterlitz-Thouless phase at sufficiently low activity.
status_evidence.claim: Classical rigorous results establish the BKT phase but do not exhibit intermediate transitions visible in correlation functions.
